task.title: Relics: add relics to the web board
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

Until now relics are reached only from the command line. This story adds them to `workbook serve`. The desktop app loads the same pages, so it gets them too.

## What this delivers

- A Relics page: a list with type and retired filters, and a page for one relic.
- A relic page shows the enforced fields, properties, parts in order, links going out and coming in, and history with diffs.
- A task's page shows the relics and parts linked to it.
- The same data over the local web API, so a project can build its own viewer.

## How content is drawn

- Workbook draws what it understands: the enforced fields, Markdown bodies, and fields as labeled values.
- A viewer reads a body's format label to decide how to draw it. Other bodies are shown as text.
- Stored HTML is shown as source and is never run inside Workbook.
- **Any body can be opened by itself in a new browser tab**, where an HTML body is drawn as a page. In the desktop app this opens the default browser.
- **The opened tab is cut off from the board.** A script inside a stored body must not be able to read or change Workbook data or call the local API. A relic written by a teammate has to be safe to open. Prove this with a test that a script in an opened body cannot reach the API.

## Rules that matter

- The page follows the existing board conventions, including the global `[hidden]` rule and usable layouts at real viewport sizes.
- The page reads through the index and never walks Git history to draw a list.
- Editing relics on the web is not part of this story unless it falls out cheaply. Reading comes first.

## Done when

- A person can browse relics, open one, follow a link to a task and back, and read a diff, all in the browser.
- An HTML body opens in a new tab and cannot reach Workbook data.
- The pages work in the desktop app.
- The pages are checked at phone and desktop widths in a real browser.
- The reference documents the page and the API routes.

## Where the design is

This story builds the part "Web" of the design relic WB-R-01M8EVZ9BQR7GNFYPYHSVT6FRC, part 01M8EVZ9BQ20NDMR0F09K3CGXB.

Read it with `workbook relic show 'WB-R-01M8EVZ9BQR7GNFYPYHSVT6FRC#01M8EVZ9BQ20NDMR0F09K3CGXB' --body`.
